back: An area covered by shallow water or with saturated soil for all or part of the year, with plants and animals adapted to wet conditions.
A shallow, grassy, seasonally waterlogged hollow, usually at the head of a stream.
Marsh: shallow water with reeds and sedges. Swamp: wetland with trees or papyrus. Floodplain: flat land beside a river flooded in the wet season.

front: Why is a wetland called a sponge?
back: It soaks up water in the wet season and releases it slowly, keeping streams flowing and reducing flood peaks.

front: How does a wetland purify water?
back: Slow flow lets silt settle; plants and bacteria take up nutrients and some pollutants.
The international wetlands treaty signed in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran; countries list Wetlands of International Importance and promise wise use.
For example Monavale Vlei (Harare) and Mana Pools (Zambezi valley).
Drainage, cultivation, building, pollution, overgrazing and burning, brick moulding and over-abstraction of water.

front: Which body approves activities on wetlands in Zimbabwe?
back: The Environmental Management Agency (EMA), under the Environmental Management Act.
